version.changelog: After you update, run twelvetake-reaper-mcp --install-bridge. If REAPER is running the 1.7.8 bridge or later, you don't have to do anything in REAPER. If you installed with ReaPack, synchronize your packages instead. Fixed: - On macOS and Linux, a tool call could occasionally time out even though REAPER was idle. The server creates each request file first and writes the request into it a moment later. If the bridge read the file in between, it found it empty and deleted it. The request never reached REAPER, so the call waited until it timed out. The bridge now leaves an empty request file in place and answers the request once the server has written it. Windows was not affected. On macOS and Linux, the server now requires bridge 1.9.4 or later. *(Reported with the fix by Kaan Özkan (@ozzaii) in issue #23.)* - The error for an out-of-date bridge told you to re-run the bridge in REAPER, even when that wasn't needed. A running bridge at version 1.7.8 or later reloads itself when --install-bridge replaces it. The error now gives the command to run, or tells you to synchronize your packages when REAPER runs the bridge from ReaPack.
